title: [CQ-C02] Bounded repository source provider
description:
Objective: Retrieve source/patterns/callers/config/tests from immutable manifests with bounded time, bytes and concurrency.

Deliverable: Bounded repository source provider. This is task C02 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): C01, R09.

implementationPlan.description: Tests first: add minimal real-Git regressions to the existing literal-search describe/fixture (no mocked argv-only proof). (A) Build a populated ACTIVE submodule containing a unique hello match under a parent with its own hello match; commit the gitlink and .gitmodules, set parent local submodule.recurse=true. Reuse fixture plumbing and scrubbed git closure; materialize child under the temp root and use test-only local file transport if submodule add is needed. Assert unscoped search contains exactly the parent match, never sub/s.txt, plus explicit sub/s.txt read and sub scope still refuse reason submodule. Exercise directory scope too if placing the populated gitlink under that directory; do not use an unpopulated gitlink that makes removal of the flag vacuously green. (B) Commit a.ts containing hello; create only an UNTRACKED .gitattributes with `a.ts -diff` afterward. Assert search at the same immutable commit still serves the exact path/line/text and bytes, complete true. (C) Commit a NUL blob with the literal on the SAME matched line (e.g. Buffer.from('bin\0hello\n')); search it and assert status truncated, reason undecodable-match, matches [], bytes 0, complete false. These may be two compact tests with a binary subcase. Assert fixture preconditions so tests cannot pass due to an inactive submodule or accidentally committed attributes. Use os.tmpdir/path.join, no symlink privilege/network dependency, private scrubbed Git env/null device on Windows vs Unix, and guaranteed cleanup.
implementationPlan.note:
Added three real-Git regressions to the 'literal searches and aggregate bounds' describe, right after the grep.column test. They reuse the scrubbed fixture closure, temp roots and afterEach cleanup, and need no network, file transport or symlink privilege.

The three tests:
- (A) 'never serves matches from a populated submodule when local submodule.recurse is enabled'.
  - Setup: a child repo initialised at src/sub, with its blob, tree and commit built by hash-object, mktree and commit-tree. The committed gitlink and .gitmodules sit next to a worktree .gitmodules. Local config sets submodule.sub.active=true and submodule.recurse=true.
  - Precondition: a raw recursing `git grep -l` lists both src/a.ts and src/sub/s.txt, so the setup cannot pass with an inactive or unpopulated submodule.
  - Assertion: the unscoped ('all') and 'src' directory-scoped ('dir') searches serve exactly the parent match. Scope src/sub and read src/sub/s.txt stay refused with reason 'submodule'.
- (B) 'serves committed text matches despite an untracked -diff attribute'.
  - Preconditions: check-attr reports `diff: unset`, and ls-tree shows only a.ts in the commit.
  - Assertion: the exact served item ({a.ts, 2, 'hello'}, bytes 9) and complete:true.
- (C) 'reports a NUL-containing binary match line explicitly instead of an empty success'.
  - Setup: b.bin is 'bin\0hello\n'.
  - Assertion: the exact item is truncated with reason undecodable-match, matches [] and bytes 0, and complete is false.

RED run on the unfixed provider: fresh `git archive HEAD` (1f9c7d5) in /tmp/moe-c02r3.hx4CVW, with this test overlaid (cmp-checked) and the lockfile-equal Linux-native node_modules symlinked. It ran under env -i with a Linux-only PATH: `vitest run src/context/repositorySource.test.ts` exits 1 with 3 failed / 130 passed (red.log). Each test failed for the expected reason:
- (A): 'all' and 'dir' both served src/sub/s.txt 'hello from SUBMODULE';
- (B): served with matches [] and bytes 0;
- (C): served-empty with no reason.

The preconditions passed.

Verified OK:

Defect A, DoD 'Root/symlink escape is refused.':
- Cause: repo-local `submodule.recurse=true` makes `git grep <commit>` recurse into populated, active submodules. git-config documents that submodule.recurse applies to grep.
- Result: provider at fcc0a4e, real git 2.43, unscoped search 'hello' with gitlink `sub`. It returns status served and complete true, and the matches include {path:'sub/s.txt', line:1, text:'hello from SUBMODULE'}.
- Why it matters: reads and scopes at or under a gitlink are refused with 'submodule', but search serves exactly those bytes. The submodule's `.git` gitfile is a worktree file and can point outside the root.
- Fix: verified that `--no-recurse-submodules` stops the recursion even with the config set.

Defect B, DoD 'Partial/missing source remains explicit.':
- Cause: `-I` decides binary from attributes, which come from the working tree/index (even an untracked .gitattributes), .git/info/attributes, local core.attributesFile and diff.<driver>.binary.
- Result: provider at fcc0a4e with an untracked `.gitattributes` containing `a.ts -diff` (git status `?? .gitattributes`). A search scoped to the committed a.ts, which contains 'hello', returns status served, matches [] and complete true. That is a false negative caused by uncommitted bytes, which breaks 'committed-bytes-only'.
- Fix: with `-a`/`--text`, git never consults attributes, so a.ts matches. A binary blob's record then contains a NUL, so the existing guard makes it explicit truncated/undecodable-match.

Repros:
- /tmp/qa-c02r2-harness/{probe-sub.sh, probe-attrs2.sh, probe-config.sh}
- Provider end-to-end probe, in a scratch copy and not the shared tree: /tmp/qa-c02r2-e2e.hY99zc/repo/packages/moe-daemon/src/context/qaProbe.test.ts

issues.description: Add --no-recurse-submodules to the grep argv. With repo-local submodule.recurse=true, an unscoped or directory search serves sub/s.txt (status served) from a populated submodule that reads and scopes refuse as 'submodule'. The flag is verified to work while the config is set. Real-Git test: an active, populated gitlink `sub` plus `git config submodule.recurse true` gives no sub/ match. Dropping the flag must fail the test.

-I reads 'binary' from attributes in the worktree, the index, info/attributes and local config, so an untracked `.gitattributes` line `a.ts -diff` makes a search of committed a.ts return served with matches []. Use -a/--text instead: binary records then contain NUL and become undecodable-match. Real-Git tests: (1) with untracked -diff, the match is still served; (2) a NUL blob containing the literal gives truncated, not served-empty; (3) restoring -I fails them.

Rejected for one silent-failure defect, one unpinned guard, and size:
(1) DoD 'Partial/missing source remains explicit': the project's local Git config can change grep's output shape, and the provider then serves corrupted match text as status 'served'. Confirmed with real git 2.43.
(2) A mutant that drops `--literal-pathspecs` from the grep argv survives all 189 focused tests. The ls-tree mutant is equivalent, because ls-tree does not glob, so it needs no test.
(3) Net 936 LOC with no CQ-C size-exception rail. Route this through a rail exception, not a re-slice.
Everything else passed, so keep the fix small. Then re-run `npm test` fresh and supply its output.

issues.description: Local repo config isn't masked. With `git config grep.column true` in the project, git 2.43 prints `<commit>:<path>\0<line>\0<col>\0<text>\n`. parseMatches folds the column into text, and the item comes back SERVED with text "1\u0000hello" (QA real-git probe). Fix: pass `--no-column` in the grep argv, and treat a NUL in decoded match text as undecodable-match. Add a real-git fixture test with grep.column=true.

Removing `--literal-pathspecs` from the grep argv survives all 189 focused tests. The 'does not interpret literal or pathspec metacharacters' case has no sibling the glob could match. Without the flag, real git also matches `literal1.ts` for scope `literal[1].ts`. Add a committed sibling `literal1.ts` containing `-hello` and assert exactly one match. The ls-tree mutant is equivalent (ls-tree doesn't glob), so no test is needed there.
